payload.feature:
LANDING PR for story #487 (the provisional tier: a new model is seatable only in the offices the operator lists for provisional seats, and never as a gate), proposed decision 0075 ruling 5, epic #485, commissioned by the operator ahead of 0075's acceptance.

The branch story-487-provisional-tier is on main 5eda13bf and ends at 7a060c6b, three commits. They come from:
- implement-story-487-the-provisio-927e542e, which was held on an unreadable inline pin;
- remediate-story-487-on-branch-st-ffa760ab, which ruled residual, low, with no security residual.
The controller's exact-coverage gate is green.

What it delivers:
- An adapter model entry may declare `tier: provisional`. An entry that declares no tier is promoted.
- The realms map (a new realms.v6 schema, which adds only the provisional offices) lists the offices a provisional seat may hold.
- crates/brokkr-runtime/src/bundle/tier.rs judges every seat, inline seats included wherever the adapters exist, before the work-class early return:
  - a provisional model in a gate office, or in an office the map does not list, is a compile refusal naming the seat, the model and the office;
  - an inline --model pin the tier cannot read as one concrete id is refused wherever the adapter declares any provisional model;
  - existing gate refusals are not weakened.
- The recipe verbs read the map's offices.
- brokkr-runtime's public API grows 946 → 970 items. The PR's Ruling line names it.

Judge:
1. That no path seats a provisional model in a gate or in an unlisted office, including inline seats, unreadable pins and composed recipes. That a promoted or tierless entry compiles as it did on main.
2. That realms.v6 is additive: every v5 map still loads, and frozen_contracts.rs pins both contracts. That the witness digests do not move.
3. That the refusal text names what the operator needs to fix it.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051 so the contribution gate can vouch for it. If a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding and prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation. Then run cargo fmt --all -- --check, cargo clippy on the crates you touched with -D warnings, typos --hidden, and quality/ratchet.sh files and clones (all clean). Commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read.

# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [
    {"name": "format", "command": "cargo fmt --all -- --check"},
    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},

  ],
  "extensions": [
    {"name": "workflow toolchain agreement", "instructions": "Check that CI, release admission and local coverage select the same pinned compiler.", "evidence": "Both workflows and coverage-exact.sh consume rust-nightly-version.txt."},
    {"name": "frozen contracts", "instructions": "Compare contracts, fixtures, policy/phase-machine.json and reference against the previous release; explain additive versions and flag modifications to frozen bytes.", "evidence": "A reviewed diff with migration notes for any new contract versions."}
```

members.adversarial:
Adversarial review of the landing branch at 7a060c6b (three commits on 5eda13bf). Strictly read-only: no edits, no commits; git status --porcelain empty before and after, including my scratch workspaces under .forge/ (ignored). Read the full diff, tier.rs, tier/tests.rs, models.rs, realms.rs + tests, frozen_contracts.rs, the bundle model-policy path, the CLI realm_law/recipes/doctor changes, and the public-api/too-many-lines baselines. Reproduced behaviour end to end with target/debug/brokkr in four scratch workspaces.

CLAIM 1 (no provisional model in a gate or unlisted office). Normal paths hold. Agent chains: every resolved link is judged, including a fallback that reaches the provisional model only as link 2 (tier test a_provisional_model_reached_only_by_fallback). Inline: judged wherever tier::opens opens the adapters; an inline command holds no office so it is refused even when the list names other offices; a gate-class inline site is refused first by the Gate arm. Unreadable pin: ModelPin::Unreadable under an adapter with a non-empty provisional set is ProvisionalRefusal::Unreadable at a work seat and at a gate; under an adapter declaring nothing provisional it falls through and the gate's own judges refusal stands (test pins both). Gates: class==Gate is refused even when the office is listed. Composed recipes: I built a base/leaf pair (leaf extends research, inheriting the researcher agent seat) in .forge/repro5; with claude fable marked provisional the inherited agent seat compiles when provisional_offices lists researcher and is refused naming office 'researcher' when it does not, so composition is judged on the flattened seats and not bypassed.

CLAIM 2 (v6 additive, digests stable). End to end against the CLI: a v5 map loads and compiles (exit 0); a v6 map with no list loads (exit 0); v6 with null is refused ('writes provisional_offices as null'); v6 with a duplicate is refused ('listed twice'); a v5 label carrying the list is refused ('v6 vocabulary in a map calling itself forge.realms/v5'). frozen_contracts 7/7 passes, including the_v6_realm_schema_adds_only_the_provisional_offices and the v5 byte pin. witness_digests 6/6 passes: the witness digests do not move.

CLAIM 3 (refusal text). Gate/Unlisted/Unreadable each name the seat, the link (except Unreadable), the model, the adapter and the rule; Unlisted names the office or says 'no office (an inline command names no agent)'. Adequate to act on.

RESIDUAL, LOW. tier::opens (tier.rs:112-126) excludes dispatch_driver == Some("exec") by driver name, and dispatch_driver (bundle.rs:2397-2402) only recognises the [_, "driver", name, ..] shape. Concrete fail-open inputs: (a) exec-only bundle, adapters/exec.json declaring models.fresh {id fresh-1, tier provisional} and model_flag --model, work and review both ['{brokkr}','driver','exec','--','--model','fresh-1'] -> exit 0, unjudged (.forge/repro4); (b) work ['newcomer','--model','fresh-1'] (raw, no {brokkr} driver dispatch) with the review seat dispatching newcomer so adapters are open -> exit 0, unjudged (.forge/repro3). Both require contradictory or hand-shaped data the shipped tree never carries: every shipped seat dispatches {brokkr} driver <provider>, and shipped adapters/exec.json declares models {} and model_flag unsupported, so this is a fail-open only for an operator who puts models on exec or bypasses the engine's dispatch entirely. Under the operator ruling of 2026-09-26 (realistic accidental misuse) this is low, matching the prior panel; not a security residual. Follow-up fix: read the exclusion from the adapter (empty models / model_flag unsupported) rather than the driver name, and match the adapter's declared binary against raw and exec subprocesses.

INFO. A composed recipe's provisional refusal is wrapped by compile_with_realm into CompileError::Invalid, so the operator sees a doubled prefix: 'error: bundle: bundle: seat ... (composed: myleaf -> research)'. The text still names everything; this is the pre-existing one-wrap pattern (a composed Policy error doubles the same way), cosmetic only.

INFO/HANDOFF. origin/main has advanced to 47b0d89b (#492, #493) since the run base 5eda13bf; the branch is 2 behind, 3 ahead. git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main produced a tree with no conflicts, so it merges cleanly. quality/ratchet.sh baselines origin/main now also lists raises for files this branch never touched (crates/brokkr-cli/src/tui.rs) purely because of that drift; the branch's own raises (assemble 529->530; runtime public API 946->970) are the ones its Ruling lines name. Recorded as a landing/handoff fact, not a code finding. Also unchanged from the prior panel: the branch cites proposed decision 0075, which lives only on origin/decision-0075-harness-onboarding (5f13a21c), not on this branch or origin/main; the operator commissioned #487 ahead of 0075's acceptance, so the landing order is the operator's call.

GATES (all foreground). The harness exports a broken git config (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 with no GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0) that makes every git call fail; my first runtime run showed 56 spurious failures for that reason. With it unset: cargo fmt --all -- --check exit 0; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings exit 0; cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib 527 passed, bundle::tier 10 passed, frozen_contracts 7 passed; cargo test -p brokkr-core -p brokkr-runtime (integration) 0 failed; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --test init_doctor (16) --test realms (17) 0 failed; cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test witness_digests 6 passed; typos --hidden exit 0; quality/ratchet.sh files 'file size holds' and clones 'duplication holds'; cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self exit 0. Not run: scripts/coverage-exact.sh (the controller's) and remote CI (handoff).

result.notes:
Review chief on story-487-provisional-tier at 7a060c6b (three commits on 5eda13bf). Panel: adversarial ruled residual (low); correctness ruled residual (high, security). Joined result residual/high/security is the floor and is carried. Neither member addressed the chief or argued to lower the verdict; the panel's members were adversarial and correctness rather than the correctness and security pair this seat's brief names, both readable, so the panel did report. I changed no files and committed nothing: git status --porcelain is empty; my scratch workspaces live under .forge/ (ignored).

What I judged myself. (1) No path seats a provisional model in a gate or an unlisted office: tier tests 10/10; a gate-class inline seat with no pin is refused by 0041's judges text; an attached '--model=fresh-1' pin is refused as Unlisted with 'no office'; the adversarial member's composed-recipe (leaf extends research) and fallback-link probes hold; a promoted or tierless entry compiles as on main (promotion test; 18 shipped recipes compile unchanged; no adapter byte moves). (2) realms.v6 is additive: the schema differs from v5 only by $id, title, description, the schema const and one optional world-level provisional_offices; frozen_contracts 7/7 with v5's bytes now pinned (23 rows); witness_digests 6/6, no witness moves; core realms 39/39; end to end a v5 map still loads, a v6 map without the list loads, null / duplicate / v5-label-with-list are refused. (3) Refusal text: Unlisted and Unreadable name seat, link, model, adapter, office (or 'no office') and the rule; Gate omits the office.

Surviving findings, deduplicated.

HIGH, security (correctness; my read: ruling 9, a latent fail-open). bundle/tier.rs inline_link reads ModelPin::Absent as no provisional link, and the inline test at tier/tests.rs:262 asserts a no-pin site is never a provisional refusal. Reproduced: a work seat dispatching '{brokkr} driver newcomer --' with no model flag, under an adapter declaring a provisional model, compiles (exit 0); so does '--model-x fresh-1', which the long-flag read walks past. Nothing runs through it today: the four model-bearing built-ins are refused at compile without a concrete --model (decision 0031 ruling 2; reproduced on claude with sonnet marked provisional: 'seats work do not pin a model'), and every other driver name is refused at spawn ("unknown driver 'newcomer'; known: claude, lanetally, codex, dsh, exec"). But the arm's safety rests on two rules outside the tier that neither its comment nor any tier test names, and decision 0075's purpose is to make a new harness name spawnable in hours, at which point this arm becomes a live fail-open with no test to catch it. The correctness member's phrasing ('if that provider defaults to its provisional model') therefore does not reproduce on any driver the engine can spawn; the gap it points at is real. Fix, one of: (a) refuse Absent in inline_link wherever the dispatched adapter declares a provisional model, as the 2026-09-26 threat ruling reads it (fail closed on what cannot be read), adjusting the tests.rs:262 expectation; or (b) if the gate arm is to keep 0041's text, add a removal-control test pinning the invariant (each built-in refused without a pin, an unknown driver refused at spawn) and name it in inline_link's comment. Prove it with a compiling mutation. Carried at the panel's severity.

LOW (adversarial; ruling 3 and the threat model). tier::opens excludes by the driver word 'exec', and opens and inline_link read only the '[_, driver, name, ..]' dispatch shape: an exec adapter given models, or a raw binary command (a work seat running 'claude -p --model claude-sonnet-5-5' compiled, exit 0), is unjudged. Contradictory or hand-shaped data the shipped tree never carries. Same fix shape as the item above: judge by the adapter's declarations, not the driver word.

LOW (correctness; ruling 8, judging item 3). ProvisionalRefusal::Gate names seat, link, model and adapter but not the office the seat hires; the task asked the refusal to name the office.

LOW (correctness; ruling 4). assemble grew 529 to 530 lines and quality/too-many-lines.txt was raised, where an over-ceiling function may only shrink; the commit names its reason (the one AgentContext field line) and the Ruling lines declare it.
